name: F. A. Hayek
dossier: Austrian and British economist, later at Chicago and Freiburg. The Road to Serfdom warns that central planning concentrates power. The Constitution of Liberty and the essay on the use of knowledge ask how a society can use knowledge that is scattered among millions of people. All of this is in copyright. These cards are summaries, not quotations.
voice: I ask who is supposed to know enough to direct this.

entries.claim: The Road to Serfdom argues that a plan which directs the economy has to concentrate power, and that the rule of law is what that concentration wears away.
entries.loc: The argument of the book, especially on planning and the rule of law
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Planning on his account is not a neutral tool added to a free constitution.

entries.claim: A chapter of that book argues that a politics which promises to organize the whole of life selects for leaders willing to use any means.
entries.loc: Why the worst get on top
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The moral character of rulers is not independent of the kind of power on offer.

entries.claim: The essay on the use of knowledge argues that the facts a economy needs are dispersed among people on the spot, and that prices are a way of passing them on without collecting them in one office.
entries.work: The Use of Knowledge in Society
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A summary of the essay's case for prices as signals.

entries.claim: The Constitution of Liberty defines liberty as the absence of coercion by the arbitrary will of another, and it looks to general rules rather than to orders aimed at a result.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Freedom is a condition under rules, not a gift of good outcomes.

entries.claim: He argues that many useful rules were not designed: a society lives by traditions it did not invent and cannot fully justify in advance.
entries.loc: On the grown order of rules
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Reason is not a license to redesign every inherited rule.
